1313: Shion is Mion's identical twin sister, who currently resides in Okinomiya. In spite of their different personalities, she and Mion often switch places, and it can be difficult to distinguish between them.
1427: Rena is a girl who returned from Ibaraki to Hinamizawa one year ago and now is in the same grade level as Keiichi. She is very kind and capable and takes care of Keiichi and her friends whenever possible, but is also naive and is usually subject to light teasing by Keiichi.
1534: Rika Furude is one of the younger students in Keiichi's school, and is in the same grade level as Satoko. Naturally, she is great friends with her, as they live together in the same house.
1611: Mion is the oldest kid in Keiichi Maebara's class. As the elder, she is the class president and everyone looks up to her as the leader. She acts like a perverted tomboy and calls herself old man, but has a hidden girlish side.
1612: Satoko is a younger classmate in Keiichi's school. She has a distinctive style of speech, ending all of her sentences with 'wa' which, at times, is grammatically incorrect. In spite of her young age, she is quite clever in setting up traps, and likes to practice on Keiichi.
1851: Keiichi is the son of a famous and extremely wealthy artist and has recently moved to Hinamizawa after an array of unfortunate events in his hometown.
1852: Satoshi is the older brother of Satoko Houjou. Although he is currently missing, his past influence is the key to the actions of several characters in Higurashi. Similar to Satoko, he cannot distinguish the difference between cauliflower and broccoli.
3128: Hanyuu is the mysterious "transfer student" in Matsuribayashi-hen. She has a pair of dark colored horns on her head, one of which is chipped slightly (however, no one seems to notice or mention them, with the exception of Takano, who calls her a "monster").
3775: Kuraudo Oishi is a veteran police investigator at Okinomiya who has vowed to solve the mystery of the Hinamizawa murders before his retirement, due to personal reasons.
4934: Miyo is a nurse at the village clinic who has a keen interest in Hinamizawa's past and culture, recording all her speculation in notebooks. At times, her storytelling can be very mysterious and chilling—she seems to enjoy putting people on edge.
6478: Toshiki is the grandson of the chief of the dam's construction. In episode 14, he is kidnapped by some anonymous guys.
6696: Rumiko is the female teacher of Keiichi's class, who is a parody character of Tsukihime's Ciel-Senpai (permission for her usage was given by Type-Moon). The seiyū for her character in the anime series is the same as the seiyū of Ciel from the Tsukihime anime.
7183: He is a young police investigator at the Metropolitan Police Department in Tokyo. He befriended Rika while investigating a case in Hinamizawa four years ago, all due to a prophecy about his wife which came true, though he just brushed it off as coincidence.
7243: A mysterious member of "Tokyo" who offers her assistance to Takano.
7445: Kyosuke is the head doctor of the village clinic. Despite his young age and the fact that he has a severe maid fetish, he is highly respected in the community. He cheerfully makes house calls and seems to truly care about everyone's health.
9464: Teppei is Satoko and Satoshi's uncle/foster father. He and his wife were forced to take care of Satoko and Satoshi after the death of their parents, but they abused them. He currently lives in Okinomiya.
9481: Oryou is the grandmother of Mion and Shion as well as the current head of the Sonozaki family. Although usually harsh and vulgar during her dealings with people, she has a bit of a softer side that she rarely lets out.
10024: A photographer who frequently visits the village of Hinamizawa (especially during the Watangashi Festival). Not much else is known about his personality.
10741: Rina is a woman who appears in Rena's life in the story Tsumihoroboshi-hen. She is the lover of Teppei Houjou, and together they swindle men out of their money through intimidation and blackmail schemes.
11840: A mysterious witch who appears to Battler following the first game, providing advice and telling him she will support him in his endeavors to solve the mystery of the witch Beatrice.
11935: Daughter to Oryou and mother to the Sonozaki sisters, she leads the Sonozaki family despite being disinherited for marrying an outsider.
14928: Tatsuyoshi is an employee of the Sonozaki family, who looks like a secret agent. He was more active in the past, but has settled down to become Shion's caretaker. He somehow knows both Teppei and Rina, and is aware of their lifestyles and badgering tactics.
14929: Head of one of the Three Families, and the official village chief of Hinamizawa. He seems to be a kindly old man, but is vehement in his hatred for Hinamizawa's enemies. His position as chief is largely symbolic as Oryou Sonozaki holds power over most of Hinamizawa.
21243: He is the president of Okonogi gardening, and can occasionally be seen doing pruning at the Hinamizawa branch school.
21244: Amakusa is a hot-blooded and open young man who cannot stand boredom and is hired by Okonogi as Ange's bodyguard. He stands by Ange's side despite being originally hired by Eva, who grew to resent Ange. Due to his talkative nature, Eva fired him before her death.
56055: Hifumi Takano is the adoptive grandfather of Takano Miyo, formerly Tanashi Miyoko. He was a researcher and a doctor during World War II, and discovered the Hinamizawa Syndrome while researching cases of psychosis preceding death during the war.
212187: A woman with horns not unlike Hanyuu's.
236530: Maebara Aiko is Maebara Keiichi's mother. She first appears in Onikakushi-hen along with her husband, Maebara Ichirō. She is rarely seen or fully depicted in the first two seasons of the anime, but she appears various times throughout the manga adaptations.
236531: Ichirou Maebara is a character in the Higurashi no Naku Koro ni series, Aiko Maebara's husband, and Keiichi Maebara's father and the builder of the Maebara House. He works as an artist and is seemingly very fond of young girls.
